near-degenerate-block.title: Coupling keeps the levels apart
near-degenerate-block.caption: At the stated bare splitting 0.20 eV, the two coupled energies are about 4.81972 and 5.18028 eV. Coupling stays at 0.15 eV throughout this graph.

gaussian-trial-energy.title: A width balances two energy costs
gaussian-trial-energy.caption: Narrow shapes cost more kinetic energy; wide shapes cost more potential energy. At width ratio 1, the total is 0.20 eV. This is a trial family, not an exact solution.

finite-rectangular-pulse.title: Contributions can cancel during one pulse
finite-rectangular-pulse.caption: For the fixed 2 s weak pulse, gap frequency π/2 rad/s gives probability about 0.00405. The zeros come from cancellation over the pulse.

weak-versus-rabi.title: The simple estimate works near zero
weak-versus-rabi.caption: The lines are very close at angle 0.10. As the angle grows, the square estimate pulls away from the exact repeating rule.

stimulated-balance-inversion.title: Increasing the drive approaches one half
stimulated-balance-inversion.caption: With spontaneous rate fixed at 0.2/ns, stimulated rate 0.3/ns gives excited fraction 0.375. This model never puts more than half in the excited state.

partial-wave-resonance.title: The full half-height width is 2 meV
partial-wave-resonance.caption: The peak at 100 meV is about 4π nm². At 99 and 101 meV it is half as high, in the constant-wave-number approximation.

gaussian-born-example.title: Scattering fades with momentum transfer
gaussian-born-example.caption: At the dimensionless input 2, the angular cross section is about 0.000680269 nm²/sr. This curve assumes the stated Born model applies.
